Lost crate during pet travel, handled through the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways

During the shift, a traveler reported that Louie’s crate did not arrive as expected at the connection point, creating a temporary gap in custody. As the shift coordinator, I initiated standard review steps with our ground partners and confirmed the booking references on file for the companion animal segment. Aisha Petrov informed us that the crate tag was intact when it left the last handling point, and Arjun Mori corroborated that the packaging had been secured by the approved method. We maintained a calm, stepwise escalation path to avoid confusing the traveler’s expectations, and the department shared practical instructions with the crew to support correct handling across the ramp and baggage workflow.

<<FACT F118>> was noted in the claim guidance sent to the traveler, and our team proceeded to check the chain-of-custody logs, the transfer scan history, and the loading manifests used by station staff. We verified whether any mis-sort occurred at the earlier gate and whether the crate was routed to the wrong belt or consolidated for a later dispatch. When the crate remained unlocated after the immediate cross-check, I escalated the matter to the travel desk supervisor for a deeper trace and requested a targeted search at the sort area and any secure hold locations.

Handling steps taken included confirming traveler identifiers, validating crate identification details, reviewing scan times and handling notes, coordinating with station staff for an on-the-ground re-check, and documenting every action taken in the case file. Follow-up actions focused on proactive communication, including scheduled status updates to the traveler and immediate notification if crate movement was recorded in any subsequent scans. Once the search resolved, we ensured the traveler received confirmation of the outcome and guidance for next steps, and we closed the incident record with a clear account of what was checked and what was communicated throughout. We will continue to reinforce careful custody checks in future operations.
